Langley is two municipalities sharing one condo market: the City of Langley, a compact urban city around 200 Street, 56 Avenue and the Fraser Highway, and the Township of Langley surrounding it, so a condo's tax rate, bylaws and development plan depend on which side of the municipal line it sits.

The City of Langley's condo core is the downtown and Fraser Highway corridor, where the City's amenity-contribution policy notes densities are already rising with SkyTrain under construction, while Township condos cluster in Willoughby and Walnut Grove, a different plan area entirely.
School District No. 35 (Langley) covers both municipalities, so school catchment does not change at the City and Township line even though taxes and bylaws do.

New seniors supply in Langley has come as housing-society and provincial product, not strata condos: British Columbia Housing announced more seniors housing opening in Langley, which is rental or supportive product a condo buyer should not count as purchase stock.

The City of Langley treats multi-family homes as one utility class — townhouse, apartment and condo together — in its 2026 utility insert, which matches how the older low-rise condo stock here is serviced and billed.

blocks.text: Langley 55+ Condos: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Development cost is a City of Langley rule a new-build buyer meets indirectly: the City's Amenity Contributions and Density Bonusing Policy CO-80 collects cash-in-lieu from multi-unit developments, with rates rising by floor-area ratio and updates on January 1, 2025 and January 1, 2026 tied in the policy to SkyTrain construction and rising densities.

The same policy lets Council consider reducing or waiving amenity contributions for affordable housing units, which is why some Langley seniors and affordable projects proceed as rental housing-society product rather than strata condos.

blocks.text: Langley 55+ Condos: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Langley City collects tax for many other bodies on one notice: its annual report lists provincial school taxes, TransLink, Metro Vancouver, British Columbia Assessment, the Downtown Langley Business Association and the Municipal Finance Authority as the other 42% of the bill, so a condo owner disputing a line is often disputing another government's levy, not the City's.

Utility money mostly leaves the City: Metro Vancouver takes 58% of Langley City water charges and 57% of sewer charges in 2026, per the City's own utility insert, so condo utility rises track regional treatment costs.

blocks.text: Langley 55+ Condos: development and new projects

items.t: British Columbia Housing seniors housing in Langley: provincial seniors housing announced as opening in Langley through British Columbia Housing. STATUS: opening announced on the British Columbia Housing release read 2026-11-03; project name, address and unit count are to be confirmed on that release before use (check current).

SkyTrain extension into Langley City: the City's amenity policy treats SkyTrain as now under construction and ties its January 1, 2025 and January 1, 2026 contribution-rate updates to that construction and to rising residential densities.

The City of Langley's 2026 total residential property tax rate is $4.2067 per $1,000 of taxable value, built on its rate summary from a City general rate plus Metro Vancouver, school, TransLink (Greater Vancouver Transportation Authority), British Columbia Assessment and Municipal Finance Authority components.

City of Langley utilities for multi-family homes rose in 2026, with water up 7.44% and sewer up 5.07% for townhouse, apartment and condo homes, and single-family solid waste up 10.49%, per the City's 2026 utility insert.

TransLink is a levy on every Langley tax notice, listed by the City among the bodies it collects for, which is the City's own confirmation that Langley condos sit inside the TransLink service and taxing area even before SkyTrain opens.

blocks.text: Langley 55+ Condos: risks and due diligence

items.t: The two-municipality split is the first risk: City and Township condos carry different tax rates, utility structures and development plans, so a buyer comparing two Langley condos must confirm the municipality for each before comparing carrying costs.
